features.description: Project scaffold: Manifest V3 extension with TypeScript, esbuild build, eslint, vitest and a minimal service worker, plus README, CHANGELOG, .gitignore and version 0.1.0 in package.json only.
steps: `npm run build` produces dist/ containing manifest.json, background service worker, popup and options pages
manifest.json is generated/copied from package.json version (version written in one place only)
`npm run lint` and `npm test` run without prompts and pass (at least one trivial passing test)
node_modules/ and dist/ are git-ignored; package-lock.json is committed
README explains what it does, how to build, and how to load dist/ via chrome://extensions (unpacked)

features.description: Settings module: typed settings (enabled, idle minutes before discard, whitelist domains, protect pinned/audible/form-dirty tabs) stored in chrome.storage.sync with defaults and validation.
steps: Unit test: loading with empty storage returns documented defaults
Unit test: invalid values (negative or non-numeric idle minutes) are rejected or clamped to the allowed range
Unit test: saved settings round-trip through a mocked chrome.storage
Unit test: changes in storage fire the change listener with the new settings

features.description: Discard policy (pure function): given tab info, last-active time, settings and now, decide whether a tab should be discarded and why not otherwise.
steps: Unit test: tab inactive longer than the idle threshold is eligible
Unit test: active tab, pinned tab, audible tab, already-discarded tab and chrome:// / extension pages are never eligible
Unit test: whitelisted domain (including subdomain match) is never eligible
Unit test: tab exactly at the threshold boundary has a fixed, tested outcome
Policy returns a reason code for every refusal

features.description: Background auto-discard: track tab last-active times (onActivated, onUpdated, onRemoved) and periodically (chrome.alarms) call chrome.tabs.discard on eligible tabs, surviving service worker restarts by persisting timestamps in chrome.storage.session.
steps: Unit test with mocked chrome API: after the alarm fires, only tabs the policy approves get discard called
Unit test: activating a tab resets its idle timer
Unit test: timestamps are restored from storage.session after a simulated worker restart
Unit test: removed tabs are dropped from tracking
Disabled setting means no discard is ever called
Real-browser check (listed under 'needs manual acceptance'): an idle tab becomes discarded after the threshold

features.description: Protect tabs with unsaved input: a content script reports when a page has edited form fields, and those tabs are excluded from discard.
steps: Unit test (jsdom): typing into an input/textarea marks the page dirty and sends a message; reset/submit clears it
Unit test: background policy treats a dirty tab as ineligible with reason code 'dirty'
Content script requests no host permissions beyond what the manifest declares and sends no page content, only a boolean

features.description: Popup UI: show enabled toggle, count of discarded tabs, estimated memory saved, a 'discard other tabs now' button and 'never discard this site' button.
steps: Unit test: 'discard now' sends the right message and background discards all eligible non-active tabs ignoring the idle threshold but still honoring protections
Unit test: 'never discard this site' adds the current tab's hostname to the whitelist
Unit test: popup render function shows counts given a stats object
Popup passes basic accessibility checks (labels on controls, keyboard operable) via a lint rule or test

features.description: Memory savings estimate: record per-discard estimated bytes (heuristic documented in code, since per-tab memory is not available on stable Chrome) and cumulative stats; show system memory via chrome.system.memory.
steps: Unit test: estimator returns the documented value for known inputs and never negative
Unit test: cumulative stats persist and can be reset
Estimate is labeled as an estimate in the UI
README documents the heuristic and its limits

features.description: Memory-pressure mode: when available system memory drops below a configurable percentage, discard the least recently used eligible tabs regardless of the idle threshold until pressure eases.
steps: Unit test: below threshold, LRU-ordered eligible tabs are discarded one at a time until the mocked free memory is above threshold
Unit test: above threshold, no extra discards occur
Unit test: protections (whitelist, pinned, audible, dirty, active) still hold under pressure
Setting for pressure threshold is validated and exposed in options

features.description: Options page: edit all settings and whitelist, with validation messages and import/export of settings as JSON.
steps: Unit test: submitting valid form saves via the settings module
Unit test: invalid input shows an error and does not save
Unit test: exported JSON re-imports to identical settings; malformed JSON is rejected with a message
Whitelist entries are normalized (hostnames, lowercase, no scheme/path)

features.description: Packaging and release: zip build script, CI workflow (lint, test, build, zip, SHA256), privacy statement (no data leaves the browser), permission minimization review, CHANGELOG entry.
steps: `npm run package` creates a versioned zip of dist/ and a SHA256 file
CI workflow runs lint, test, build and package on push
manifest permissions list contains only those actually used (tabs, storage, alarms, system.memory as applicable) with justification in README
A test checks that manifest.json declares no remote code, no host permissions beyond content-script needs, and no network calls exist in src/
Real-browser smoke test of the built zip is listed under 'needs manual acceptance'

verify: npm ci && npm run lint && npm test && npm run build
